Shai-Hulud hits npm and PyPI

Campaign: shai-hulud-here-we-go-again
Date: 2026-05-11 to 2026-05-19 (8 days)
Actor: TeamPCP (group)
Impact: credential_theft, self_propagation
User Impact: 200000000

Synopsis

Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again was a May 2026 TeamPCP campaign affecting roughly 169 to 170+ npm package names, plus 2 PyPI packages, with combined reported download volume above 200 million per week.

Story

The May 2026 Shai-Hulud wave was a TeamPCP campaign against package publishers, not one project. JFrog reported more than 170 npm packages and two PyPI packages; Aikido counted 373 malicious package-version entries across 169 npm names as researchers refined the list.

The npm payload used `@tanstack/setup` as a GitHub dependency, rewrote package metadata, bumped versions, and republished infected tarballs with stolen npm tokens. In GitHub Actions, it could use OIDC trusted publishing to mint an npm publish token under a legitimate workflow identity.

The malware daemonized after install so the package manager could return while harvesting continued. Its value was in recursion: a package install in a privileged developer or CI environment could expose tokens, find more publishable packages, and publish the next wave.

High-value scopes, including TanStack, Mistral, UiPath, OpenSearch prereleases, and Guardrails, are tracked separately where package evidence is precise. The campaign record holds the moving aggregate and the common mechanics.
